title: Daily tracking baselines and abnormal-move thresholds
note: Baselines, not decisions. The brain may publish a TrackingCadenceVersion that changes an adjustable interval with a reason and refs; it may never change a fixed one, and it may never skip a baseline pull. Owner instruction 2026-09-09: tracking is resident once a company has passed its Initial Screen. Owner instruction 2026-09-10: filings are part of daily tracking, management share sales and buyback announcements especially -- hence sec and sec-ownership are both here, both daily, both fixed.

cadences.because: one settled close a trading day plus an intraday provisional read; the price lane holds a company six hours after a run that added no trading day, so asking more often buys nothing and asking less often freezes an intraday print as a close

8-K and the filing calendar are checked daily whatever else is happening; a filing nobody looked for is the one event a covering analyst may not miss. This key covers the filings index and everything derived from the block it returns: the 8-K items, the earnings-release dates, and the 10-Q/10-K Item 2 issuer-purchases table once the filing itself has been fetched. US repurchases have no faster source than this -- there is no daily buyback return in America -- so the cadence that matters for a buyback is the one that notices the 10-Q on the day it lands.

Form 4 is due within two business days of the trade, so once per trading day is enough to be never more than a day behind the filer, and more often would spend the operation's quota re-reading filings that cannot have changed. Fixed rather than adjustable for the same reason the filings index is: management selling and a 13D arriving are the two things a covering analyst may not find out about late, and the brain sets rates -- it does not decide whether we look. The lane's own run covers the gap a weekend leaves: a Monday run reads the whole window back to Friday's trades, because it derives what is unread from the filings index rather than from when it last ran.

twice a day for broker reports and call minutes; thinly covered companies are where the brain should stretch this to two or three days, because a search that returns the same four documents is a search that cost a quota unit for nothing
twice a day for what the street is saying, verified by web search before anything from it is read as a fact; the owner reads this for market view, not for figures
daily, per the owner's cadence table. The notes themselves arrive about twice a day, which is why a day's pull picks up both; pulling twice would read the same file twice as often as it changes
the verification path behind a crowd post and the catch-all for company news; generic, so it runs alongside the specific sources rather than instead of them
expert call libraries turn over slowly and each read is expensive; weekly unless an event pulls it forward
the fund's own file changes when someone writes in it, which is roughly weekly
hiring and morale move over quarters; a daily read of them is noise wearing a timestamp
C1's CatalystCalendarVersion is checked every day and the brain does not get to slow it down: a date that moved and nobody looked is how a preview is written for the wrong week

abnormal_move.note: Three thresholds, any of which fires. Absolute catches a move nobody in the universe shared; excess-vs-basket is the one that matters for a five-name sector universe, because the whole sector falling four percent is not news about one company; excess-vs-benchmark only fires when a price series for the benchmark exists, and its absence is recorded rather than assumed to be zero. The divergence window is separate and slower: over ten settled trading days, a company running six points against what its thesis implies -- relative to the same equal-weight basket -- is the case the owner cares about most, because agreeing with the market is worth nothing and the interesting question is what we missed. One event per window per company; a divergence that persists does not re-fire daily.

immediate_pull.because: a price that moved without a reason is the one case where waiting for the baseline is wrong: the reason is being written now and will be harder to find in two days

thesis_stances.note: Per-thesis overrides for the divergence detector. The fund is fundamental long-biased, so an admitted coverage thesis is read as long unless it is named here; a short thesis is a line of policy, not a code change.
